--- title: "20 Famous Open Data Sources for Analytics, and How to Extract Data 🗄️" description: "The twenty best-known free data sources, from Kaggle and UCI to FRED, the World Bank, NASA and SEC EDGAR, with a filterable catalogue, extraction code for each access method and a simulated end-to-end pipeline." author: "MLStation" date: 2026-10-01 categories: [Resources, Datasets, Open Data, APIs] draft: false --- Good practice data is the fuel of every project. The twenty sources below are free, famous and reliable. Some give you a CSV with one click; others need an API call, a Python package or a SQL query. This guide shows **what each source is good for** and **exactly how to pull data from it**. 🚀 ::: {.callout-tip} ## 🎯 What you will get - 🗂️ A filterable catalogue of 20 open data sources - 🧭 A decision flow for choosing the right extraction method - 💻 Copy-ready extraction code for downloads, APIs, Python packages, SQL and cloud buckets - 🔄 An animated extract → clean → store pipeline and a worked, simulated example - ⚖️ Notes on licences, rate limits and good manners ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## 📚 The Resources hub [🧭 Overview: where to find resources](/resources/resources-overview.qmd) · [🛤️ Learning paths](/resources/learning-paths/industrial-use-case-paths.qmd) · [📝 Cheat sheets](/resources/cheat-sheets/data-science-cheat-sheets.qmd) · [📖 Glossary](/resources/glossary/data-science-glossary.qmd) · [🗄️ 20 open data sources](/resources/datasets/open-data-sources.qmd) · 📄 Paper notes (coming soon) ::: ## 🗂️ The catalogue ```{ojs} //| datasets, many with notebooks", how: "Python package / CLI", key: "Free account token", fmt: "CSV, Parquet, images", url: "https://www.kaggle.com/datasets"}, {n: 2, method: "Python package", name: noKey = Inputs.toggle({label: "🔓 Only sources needing no key or account", value: false}) ``` ```{ojs} //| echo: false shownSources = sources.filter(d => (dom === "All domains" || d.dom === dom) && The chart counts the main access method for each source. ```{ojs} //| echo: false Plot.plot({ ...msStyle, height: 260, width: 760, marginLeft: 130, x: {label: "Number of sources →", grid: true}, y: {label: null}, marks: [ Plot.barX(sources, Plot.groupY({x: "count"}, {y: "method", fill: d => d.key.startsWith("None") ? "No key needed" : "Key or account", sort: {y: "-x"}, rx: 3})), ], color: {domain: ["No key needed", "Key or account"], range: [ms.teal, ms.amber], legend: true} }) ``` ::: {.callout-note} ## 📝 Note The FRED **CSV link** works without a key, for example `fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE` ([FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE)); the full **API** needs a free key ([FRED API docs](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/)). ::: ## 🧭 Which extraction method? ```{mermaid} %%| echo: false flowchart TD A["❓ What does the source offer?"] --> B{"A download link?"} B -- yes --> C["📥 pandas.read_csv / read_parquet
straight from the URL"] B -- no --> D{"A Python package?"} D -- yes --> E["📦 ucimlrepo, datasets,
fetch_openml, earthaccess, kaggle"] D -- no --> F{"A REST API?"} F -- yes --> G["🌐 requests + JSON
pagination, keys, rate limits"] F -- no --> H{"A SQL warehouse
or cloud bucket?"} H -- SQL --> I["🗃️ BigQuery client"] H -- bucket --> J["☁️ S3 with --no-sign-request"] ``` ## 💻 Extraction recipes Each tab is a working pattern. Replace dataset codes and keys with your own. Keys belong in environment variables, never in notebooks you share. ::: {.panel-tabset} ## 📥 Direct download ```python import pandas as pd # Our World in Data: every chart has a CSV le = pd.read_csv( "https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/life-expectancy.csv") # FRED: one series, no key needed unrate = pd.read_csv( "https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE", parse_dates=["observation_date"]) # NYC TLC: copy a monthly Parquet link from the TLC page trips = pd.read_parquet(".parquet") ``` ## 📦 Python packages ```python # UCI repository from ucimlrepo import fetch_ucirepo # pip install ucimlrepo wine = fetch_ucirepo(id=109) X, y = wine.data.features, wine.data.targets # OpenML through scikit-learn from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml titanic = fetch_openml("titanic", version=1, as_frame=True).frame # Hugging Face from datasets import load_dataset # pip install datasets imdb = load_dataset("imdb", split="train").to_pandas() # Kaggle (token in ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json) # kaggle datasets download -d blastchar/telco-customer-churn --unzip ``` ## 🌐 REST APIs ```python import os, requests, pandas as pd # World Bank: no key; JSON when format=json url = ("https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/US;IN;BR" "/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD") page = requests.get(url, params={"format": "json", "per_page": 500}).json() meta, rows = page # [paging info, records] gdp = pd.json_normalize(rows)[["country.value", "date", "value"]] # FRED API: free key in an environment variable obs = requests.get( "https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations", params={"series_id": "CPIAUCSL", "file_type": "json", "api_key": os.environ["FRED_API_KEY"]}).json() cpi = pd.DataFrame(obs["observations"]) # SEC EDGAR: no key, but identify yourself hdr = {"User-Agent": "Your Name your.email@example.com"} apple = requests.get( "https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000320193.json", headers=hdr).json() ``` ## 🗺️ Geospatial ```python import requests, pandas as pd # OpenStreetMap Overpass: cafés in central Austin query = """ [out:json][timeout:25]; node["amenity"="cafe"](30.25,-97.76,30.29,-97.72); out; """ r = requests.post("https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter", data={"data": query}).json() cafes = pd.DataFrame([{"name": e["tags"].get("name"), "lat": e["lat"], "lon": e["lon"]} for e in r["elements"]]) ``` ## 🗃️ SQL (BigQuery) ```python # pip install google-cloud-bigquery ; gcloud auth application-default login from google.cloud import bigquery client = bigquery.Client(project="your-project-id") sql = """ SELECT name, SUM(number) AS babies FROM `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current` WHERE year >= 2000 GROUP BY name ORDER BY babies DESC LIMIT 10 """ top_names = client.query(sql).to_dataframe() ``` ## ☁️ Cloud buckets ```bash # AWS Open Data and Common Crawl allow anonymous access aws s3 ls s3://commoncrawl/crawl-data/ --no-sign-request # copy one file to your machine aws s3 cp s3:////file.parquet . --no-sign-request ``` ::: BigQuery gives every project the **first 1 TB of queries per month free**, and Google pays to store the public datasets ([Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/public-data)). NOAA's API needs a token in the request header and allows **5 requests per second and 10,000 per day** ([NOAA](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/cdo-web/webservices/v2)). ## 🔄 The extraction pipeline, animated Real projects wrap extraction in a small pipeline so it can be re-run safely. Press play and follow a batch of records. ```{ojs} //| echo: false viewof playPipe = Inputs.toggle({label: "▶ Play animation", value: true}) ``` ```{ojs} //| echo: false pipeState = ({t: 0}) pipeTick = { while (true) { yield pipeState.t; if (!playPipe) return; pipeState.t = (pipeState.t + 1) % 300; await Promises.delay(40); } } { const stages = [["🌐", "Extract", "API, file, SQL"], ["✅", "Validate", "schema, nulls, ranges"], ["🧹", "Clean", "types, units, duplicates"], ["💾", "Store", "Parquet, database"], ["📊", "Analyse", "charts, models"]]; const W = 780, H = 190, xs = stages.map((_, i) => 70 + i * (W - 140) / 4); const dots = d3.range(6).map(k => { const p = ((pipeTick + k * 50) % 300) / 300 * 4; const s = Math.floor(p), f = p - s; return {x: xs[s] + (xs[Math.min(4, s + 1)] - xs[s]) * f, bad: k === 2 && p > 1 && p < 1.15}; }); const active = Math.floor((pipeTick % 300) / 300 * 5); return htl.svg``; } ``` ## 🧪 Worked example: cleaning API data (simulated) APIs rarely return a tidy table. Below we **simulate** a World Bank-style JSON response for five fictional countries, with typical problems: nested fields, values as strings, missing years and one unit error. Then we clean it in a few lines. ::: {#3341a985 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} import numpy as np, pandas as pd, plotly.express as px from ms_charts import COLORS, PLOTLY_CONFIG rng = np.random.default_rng(4) # --- simulate a nested API response (fictional countries) --- countries = [("Aurelia", 120), ("Borealis", 80), ("Caldera", 45), ("Deltora", 30), ("Equinox", 15)] records = [] for c, start in countries: level = start for year in range(2005, 2026): level *= 1 + rng.normal(0.035, 0.025) # values arrive as strings, about 6% are missing v = None if rng.random() < 0.06 else str(round(level * 1e9)) records.append({"country": {"id": c[:2].upper(), "value": c}, "date": str(year), "value": v}) # one record has a unit error (1000x too big) if records[30]["value"] is None: records[30]["value"] = "1e9" records[30]["value"] = str(float(records[30]["value"]) * 1000) # --- clean --- df = pd.json_normalize(records) # flatten nested JSON df = df.rename(columns={"country.value": "country"}) df["year"] = df["date"].astype(int) df["gdp_bn"] = pd.to_numeric(df["value"]) / 1e9 # strings → numbers med = df.groupby("country").gdp_bn.transform("median") df.loc[df.gdp_bn > 20 * med, "gdp_bn"] = np.nan # drop the unit error df["gdp_bn"] = df.groupby("country").gdp_bn.transform( lambda s: s.interpolate(limit_direction="both")) # fill gaps print(f"{df.value.isna().sum()} missing values filled, 1 unit error fixed") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 2 missing values filled, 1 unit error fixed ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-gdp .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"} fig = px.line(df, x="year", y="gdp_bn", color="country", markers=True, color_discrete_sequence=[COLORS["indigo"], COLORS["teal"], COLORS["amber"], COLORS["rose"], COLORS["violet"]]) fig.update_layout(height=380, yaxis_title="GDP (billions, simulated)", xaxis_title=None, legend_title=None) fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG) ``` ::: {#fig-gdp .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Cleaned, simulated GDP series for five fictional countries. ::: ::: ## 🛡️ Be a good data citizen | Rule | Why | How | |---|---|---| | 📜 Read the licence | Some data cannot be used commercially or needs attribution | Check the source's terms page; cite it in your charts | | ⏱️ Respect rate limits | Too many calls get you blocked | Sleep between calls, use bulk downloads when offered | | 💾 Cache what you fetch | Re-downloading wastes time and quota | Save raw responses to Parquet or JSON with a date | | 🔑 Hide your keys | Leaked keys get abused | Environment variables, `.env` files in `.gitignore` | | 🧾 Record provenance | You must be able to reproduce results | Log URL, parameters and download date | | 🔐 Protect people | Even open data can identify individuals | Aggregate, drop identifiers, follow privacy rules | A small helper that caches and retries covers most needs: ```{.python filename="fetch.py"} import time, json, pathlib, hashlib, requests def fetch_json(url, params=None, cache="raw", retries=3): h = hashlib.sha1(f"{url}{params}".encode()).hexdigest()[:16] key = pathlib.Path(cache) / f"{h}.json" if key.exists(): return json.loads(key.read_text()) # cached copy for attempt in range(retries): r = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=30) if r.status_code == 429: # rate limited time.sleep(2 ** attempt); continue r.raise_for_status() key.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True) key.write_text(r.text) return r.json() raise RuntimeError("Gave up after retries") ``` ## 🧩 Summary - Start with **Kaggle, UCI, OpenML and Hugging Face** for ML practice; use **FRED, World Bank, Eurostat, Census and OWID** for economics and society; **NOAA, NASA and OSM** for climate and maps; **BigQuery, AWS and Common Crawl** for big data. - Pick the extraction method from what the source offers: **download → package → API → SQL or bucket**. - Flatten, convert, validate and **cache** what you fetch. - Follow **licences, rate limits and privacy** rules. - Put the data to work with a [learning path](/resources/learning-paths/industrial-use-case-paths.qmd) 🛤️.
